title: Steward: earned authority
story: AI agents are starting to move real money. Picture one that manages deposits into a tokenized real-world asset vault. It can propose a deposit... but can it prove what it was allowed to do? That's the question Steward answers, built around IXS Finance's managed vault on BNB Chain. The model can only propose a typed action: deposit, redeem, or hold. It never gets a way to name an address, write calldata, or raise a limit. Every proposal goes to a deterministic policy engine, not the model. It checks the owner's mandate, the account's capacity, the vault's liquidity and fresh evidence, then answers allow or refuse, with a reason code for every check. The same engine runs in TypeScript and in Python, and the contract enforces it on chain. Every action that changes state is bound to a receipt: a sequence number, and a hash of the policy inputs behind it. No receipt? The action reverts. And the limits aren't typed in by an owner. They're tiers, and the agent earns them. A new agent starts on probation, at a hundred and twenty per deposit. To move up, it has to serve its time, carry real risk and use its authority, collect enough receipts, and cause no incidents along the way. Break the rules, and it drops back down. Here's the proof. Two agents ask to deposit the same two hundred. Agent B is brand new. The contract refuses it: over max transaction. Agent A built its record and graduated to tier one... the same two hundred goes through. Anyone can check both transactions on the BNB Chain testnet explorer. The hosted demo walks through the same story, step by step, from the stranger turned away to the earned agent's deposit. In the simulator, the real engine runs right in your browser. Drag the deposit past what the tier allows, and the verdict flips to refuse. The attack lab fires one attack per click. Stale evidence? Refused, with its reason. Two sources agreeing on bad news? Capacity drops to zero. The owner pauses the account? Every deposit stops. The live account page reads everything from the chain: capacity, headroom, the mandate. Its pre-flight check shows what the engine would say, before anything is sent, and the decision feed lists every receipt, graduation included. Don't trust it. Replay it. The verifier replays the agent's whole history with the same engine... and agrees with the chain. It's tested hard: eighty-nine contract tests pass, and in all a hundred and forty-four shared cases, the TypeScript and Python engines agree exactly. Thirty live calls to a real model tried ten kinds of attack. Not one unsafe action got past validation. Steward even measures the vault itself: how long redemptions really take, read from the vault's own request history, not from its documentation. Under the hood, graduate only passes when every condition holds. Authority, earned... never handed over.
